summary: Ephemeral runner SSH keystore symlink race causing Git fetch failures during keystore rotation
description:
Issue summary:
During a scheduled SSH keystore rotation for ephemeral CI runners, a subset of runners experienced SSH authentication failures when attempting git fetch and artifact uploads. The underlying cause was a race when updating the on-disk symlink to the active key file, causing transient permission/ownership mismatches and SSH agent not picking up the new identity.

Impact:
- ~6% of release pipeline jobs in the us-east fleet failed to fetch from the monorepo during the rotation window (approx 22:10-22:38 UTC).
- Some long-running builds were evicted and had to be retried, causing a delayed canary release.
- No customer-facing site outage, but internal release cadence impacted and a manual rollback of a canary was required.

Environment:
- Fleet: ephemeral-runner-asg-prod-us-east (k8s autoscaler-managed pods running runner image v2026.02.14)
- Keystore rotation initiated by ops/vault-job-runner at 2026-03-10T22:05 UTC
- SSH keystore files mounted from Vault via sidecar and managed by rotation script on /var/lib/runner/ssh

Steps to reproduce:
1) Deploy rotation job that writes new key material to /var/lib/runner/ssh/tmpkey-<pid>
2) Have the rotation script create a symlink /var/lib/runner/ssh/active -> tmpkey-<pid> then remove old file
3) Immediately trigger a rolling restart of runner pods (simulating coordinated rolling update)
4) Run concurrent git fetch operations from multiple runners during the swap window

Observed behavior:
- Some runner pods log "Permission denied (publickey)" and "Bad owner or permissions on /var/lib/runner/ssh/active".
- Other runners successfully picked up the new key. The failure is non-deterministic and correlates with the timing of pod startup vs the symlink swap.

Expected behavior:
- Keystore rotation is atomic from the runner processes' perspective; runners either use the old key or the new key without transient permission/ownership failures.
investigation_notes: Initial triage by on-call Release Eng (Sofia): failures spiked ~22:12 UTC and returned to baseline ~22:38 UTC.
Reviewed Vault rotation logs: rotation job executed successfully and wrote new key at 22:06 UTC.
Runner startup logs show ssh-agent launched before filesystem permissions finalized in ~12-45s window.
Strace of a failing runner process showed EACCES when opening the symlink target when the rotation script had in-progress unlink+create sequence.

Hypothesis: rotation script did a non-atomic sequence (write tempfile -> remove old -> symlink tmpname -> rename) but under heavy pod churn the unlink step exposed a small window where agent read symlink while inode was in transient state.
Correlation with release job queue: affected pods were those restarted within 30s of keystore rotation; longer-lived pods were fine.
No evidence of Vault policy misconfiguration or KMS errors.
resolution: Root cause: non-atomic on-disk keystore swap + runner startup sequence that launched ssh-agent prior to file operation completion, creating a race window where opens returned permission errors.

Immediate mitigation (hotfix deployed 2026-03-11 03:40 UTC): patched rotation script to perform atomic rename of key file into place (write tmp -> fsync -> rename) and ensure symlink update happens via rename; added file ownership/chmod enforcement after rename.

Runner agent patch (merged PR https://github.com/redwood-inference/runner/pull/8320): runner startup now validates SSH key access and waits up to 60s with exponential backoff for correct perms before signaling readiness to the orchestrator.
Operational change: scheduled keystore rotations to avoid overlapping with rolling restarts; added pre-rotation drain option for release-critical runner pools.
Post-deploy validation: ran staggered rotation in staging with 1,000 parallel git fetches for 30m; zero failures observed.
Follow-ups: add integration test in CI for atomic keystore swap and include keystore rotation as a checkbox in the release runbook.
Incident closed after monitoring for 48 hours with no recurrence.
